name: Lumbar Spondylolysis
definition: A defect or stress fracture of the pars interarticularis, commonly in the lower lumbar spine; it may occur with or without vertebral slip.

typical: Pain may increase with lumbar extension
Often seen in athletes exposed to repetitive extension/loading

redFlags.item: Major neurological deficit is atypical and needs urgent alternate evaluation
High-energy trauma or systemic red flags require separate pathway

core: Neurological exam when leg symptoms are present

differentials: Stress fracture or other osseous lesion

investigations.principle: Imaging selection depends on age, duration, suspected pars lesion and neurological context.
investigations.radiographs: Can show pars-related abnormalities/slip but may miss early stress injury.
investigations.MRI: Useful for alternative pathology and selected stress-reaction assessment; CT may better define a bony pars defect when needed.

green: Relative activity modification when symptoms are load-related
amber: Bracing and operative decisions are individualized; persistent pain, high-grade slip or neurological symptoms need specialist review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Katishoola/Vata-related symptom overlap is possible but not a validated classical identity for a pars defect.

patientEducation.summary: A defect or stress fracture of the pars interarticularis, commonly in the lower lumbar spine; it may occur with or without vertebral slip.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal pain, or cancer-associated neurological symptoms.
